questions.subtopic: 1C1 Organizational governance basics. A regulator's inspectors working on site
questions.question: Two central bank inspectors now work full-time inside a Laotian bank, testing its compliance controls. Where in the Three Lines Model should internal auditor Khamla Phommachanh BEST place them?

options.A: In the third line: they test controls independently of management
options.B: In the second line: they monitor compliance from inside the bank
options.C: Outside the lines: lines are staffed by the bank's own employees
options.D: Outside the three lines: their assurance serves an outside party

questions.key_concept: Regulators' inspections, like external audit, sit outside the three lines: they serve external parties, wherever their staff work and whatever they test.
questions.pre_read: Whom do the inspectors work for? Does where they sit, or what they test, decide their place in the model?
questions.correct_explanation: The IIA's 2026 Three Lines statement lists regulators' inspections, like external audit, among providers outside the three lines: their assurance serves external parties, here the central bank that sends them. Working inside the bank, or testing compliance controls, does not move them into a line. The closest choice reads the location and the compliance testing as second-line monitoring, which is a role inside management.

wrong_explanations.B: Closest choice: compliance monitoring by the bank's own specialists is second-line work. These inspectors answer to the central bank, not to the bank's management, so they sit outside the lines.
wrong_explanations.A: The third line is the bank's own internal audit function and any third-line roles it sets up. Inspectors directed by an outside authority belong to none of its lines.
wrong_explanations.C: The verdict fits but the reason does not: outside staff the bank hires and directs can fill a line. The inspectors sit outside because their work serves the central bank.

tips: Eliminate: A, because the third line is the bank's own internal audit function and third-line roles, and C, because staff the bank hires from outside can still fill a line.
Final two: D beats B because the statement names regulators' inspections among providers outside the three lines: their work serves external parties, wherever their staff sit or whatever they test.
Exam cue: on CIA questions, external auditors and regulators sit outside the three lines, even when their staff work on site. Ask whom the work is for.

questions.subtopic: 1C3 Ethics and compliance issues. A disciplinary panel asks for the auditor
questions.question: Internal auditor Aidana Bekova reported a Kyrgyz miner's buyer for breaking its gifts rules; the HR-led panel deciding such cases under the ethics policy invites Aidana to sit on it. What is Aidana's BEST course?

options.A: Decline any part in the case, so internal audit stays objective
options.B: Brief the panel on the facts found, leaving the decision to it
options.C: Refer the request to the board, since the case concerns ethics
options.D: Point the panel to the final communication, which is due next month

questions.key_concept: Internal auditors give those with authority to act the facts behind an ethics concern; management decides discipline, so stating facts does not impair objectivity.
questions.pre_read: Does stating facts to the people who decide take a management decision? What would?
questions.correct_explanation: Standard 1.2 requires internal auditors to report ethics concerns as the organization's policies direct, here to the panel that decides such cases, and Standard 1.1 bars withholding material facts that decisions depend on. Briefing the panel does both, in line with the methodology the chief audit executive should set, while discipline stays management's decision. The closest choice withdraws to protect objectivity, but stating facts takes no management decision.

wrong_explanations.A: Closest choice: internal auditors should not sit on a body that decides discipline. Stating facts to it is reporting, and withholding them would leave the panel deciding without them.
wrong_explanations.C: The chief audit executive should take a senior manager's ethics breach to the board. A buyer's breach goes through the organization's own process, here the panel.
wrong_explanations.D: Final communications carry engagement results, but this panel is deciding now and has authority to act. The facts it needs should not wait a month.

tips: Eliminate: C, because the board route is for a senior manager's breach, not a buyer's, and D, because a body deciding the case now should not wait for a later report.
Final two: B beats A because giving facts to those with authority is reporting, which the Standards require; only deciding the sanction would cross into management's role.
Exam cue: on CIA questions, internal auditors report what they found and let management decide consequences. Stating facts does not impair objectivity; making the decision would.

questions.subtopic: 1C6 Risk management across the organization. A risk held below its escalation threshold
questions.question: A Guyanese gold miner's policy sends risks rated above 15 to its executive committee within a month. Which finding should internal auditor Shondelle Bacchus MOST clearly report as a weakness in the process?

options.A: One mine's dam risk, rated 18, reached the committee in month five
options.B: A plant accepted a risk within the board's appetite and recorded why
options.C: Every mine rates its risks on the group's single scoring scale
options.D: One mine's flood risk, rated 16, reached the committee in week three

questions.key_concept: Assessing risk management includes checking that significant risks are escalated as the organization's policy requires; a risk that arrives late shows a failing step.
questions.pre_read: What does the policy require, and by when? Which finding misses it, and which only looks risky?
questions.correct_explanation: The miner's policy is the criterion: risks rated above 15 reach the executive committee within a month. The IIA's 2026 statement on enterprise risk management says internal audit's assurance over it covers whether significant risks are passed up and reported as they should be. A risk rated 18 that reached the committee in month five shows that step failing. The closest choice is a legitimate response: recorded acceptance within appetite.

wrong_explanations.B: Closest choice: accepting a risk is a legitimate response when it stays within appetite and the decision is recorded. It becomes a concern only above appetite or tolerance.
wrong_explanations.C: One scoring scale across units is sound design, because it lets risks be compared and escalated consistently. It shows the process working, not failing.
wrong_explanations.D: Escalation in the third week meets the policy's one-month limit, so this risk shows the process working, not failing.

tips: Eliminate: C, because a single scale is what consistent rating needs, and D, because escalation within the month is what the policy requires.
Final two: A beats B because a risk above the threshold that took five months to reach the committee breaks the policy, while recorded acceptance within appetite is a sound response.
Exam cue: on CIA questions, judge risk management against its own rules and the board's appetite. A step the policy requires that is done late or not at all is an operating weakness.

questions.subtopic: 1C4 Types of risk. An organization's own risk categories
questions.question: An Australian salmon farmer's risk register groups risks as biological, market, people and license, not as strategic, operational, financial and compliance. Which view by internal auditor Kirra Watson is MOST accurate?

options.A: Deficient: the Standards' four categories are the ones a register needs
options.B: Deficient: a recognized risk framework's categories are the ones to use
options.C: Acceptable: categories have no bearing on how significant a risk is
options.D: Acceptable: the Standards name four categories but require none of them

questions.key_concept: The Standards mention strategic, operational, financial and compliance risk as categories internal auditors may consider; an organization may use its own categories.
questions.pre_read: Are the four categories a requirement or an example in the Standards? Who sets an organization's risk categories?
questions.correct_explanation: In Standard 13.2, the four categories appear only in a consideration, as examples internal auditors may consider when gathering information; none is required and none is defined. The IIA's 2026 statement on enterprise risk management has internal audit test risk identification against the organization's established taxonomy, not impose one. The closest choice turns a may into a must.

wrong_explanations.A: Closest choice: the four categories appear in a consideration, as examples internal auditors may use. They are not a structure every register must follow.
wrong_explanations.B: A recognized framework's list is a useful source, and binding where an organization has adopted it or a regulator requires it. Neither applies here.
wrong_explanations.C: The verdict fits but the reason does not: appetite can differ by type of risk, so a risk's category can change how much a gap weighs.

tips: Eliminate: B, because a framework's categories bind only where adopted or required, and C, because appetite can differ by type of risk, so categories can affect significance.
Final two: D beats A because the four categories sit in a consideration, a may, so a register grouped another way is not deficient for that reason.
Exam cue: on CIA questions, a list the Standards give in a consideration is an example, not a rule. Check the strength of the source before calling something deficient.

questions.subtopic: 1C1 Organizational governance basics. A model's option that a license condition bars
questions.question: A Bahraini insurer's license bars chief audit executive Mariam Janahi from supervising second-line work, but the chief executive, citing the Three Lines statement, asks Mariam to lead the risk team. What is Mariam's BEST response?

options.A: Accept, once the board approves the role and the charter records safeguards
options.B: Tell the board and senior management the license rules out the role
options.C: Accept for a set period, with outside assurance and a hand-back plan
options.D: Discuss the role with the chief executive, then seek the board's approval

questions.key_concept: A Statement of Position is guidance: where a license or law forbids an arrangement it allows, the binding rule wins, and the board hears why.
questions.pre_read: The Three Lines statement allows this with safeguards. What does it say about formal requirements, and what binds the insurer?
questions.correct_explanation: Standard 7.1 requires the chief audit executive to discuss any proposed role that could impair independence with the board and senior management, and Standard 1.3 requires internal auditors to abide by applicable laws and regulations. The IIA's 2026 Three Lines statement allows a chief audit executive to supervise second-line roles with safeguards but notes that formal requirements may prohibit it. Here the license does, so no safeguard makes the role acceptable.

wrong_explanations.D: Closest choice: such roles are discussed with the board and senior management, but no approval can help here, as the license bars the role. Both should hear that instead.
wrong_explanations.A: Board approval and charter safeguards fit an ongoing role that nothing forbids. A license condition binds the insurer, and board approval cannot set it aside.
wrong_explanations.C: A temporary role with outside assurance and a hand-back plan fits where the role is allowed. The license bars it for any period.

tips: Eliminate: A, because board approval cannot override a license condition, and C, because a temporary arrangement is still the role the license bars.
Final two: B beats D because the license rules the role out, so the required discussion with the board and senior management is about the bar, not about seeking approval.
Exam cue: on CIA questions, a Statement of Position is guidance. Where a law, regulation or license forbids an arrangement the guidance allows, the binding rule wins.

questions.subtopic: 1C3 Ethics and compliance issues. Requirements that come with a new activity
questions.question: A Malawian charity has sold crafts online, and counsel advises consumer and data rules bind every online seller; its compliance register lists charity-law duties alone. Which view by internal auditor Chikondi Phiri is BEST?

options.A: Complete: a charity's compliance duties are set by charity law
options.B: Complete for now, until management assesses which new rules apply
options.C: Incomplete: the online sales added duties the register omits
options.D: Incomplete: it omits good-practice codes for online sellers

questions.key_concept: The compliance requirements that apply follow what an organization does; a new activity can bring new laws and rules that its register must show.
questions.pre_read: What does the charity now do, and does a change in activity change which requirements apply?
questions.correct_explanation: In the Standards' glossary, compliance means meeting the requirements that bind the organization, from laws and regulations to its own policies. Which ones bind it depends on what it does: selling online makes the charity an online seller, and counsel advises that consumer and data rules bind every one, so a register showing charity law alone is incomplete. The closest choice describes the charity's duties before it traded.

wrong_explanations.A: Closest choice: charity law sets a charity's core duties, and it was enough before the charity traded. Selling online made it an online seller, which counsel says brings further rules.
wrong_explanations.B: Management does decide how to meet its obligations, but the duties applied from the first sale. Counsel's advice shows they exist; the register has not caught up.
wrong_explanations.D: A good-practice code binds the charity only if a law, a contract or its own policy imposes it. The gap is the rules counsel identified.

tips: Eliminate: B, because duties apply from the first sale, not from management's later review, and D, because a good-practice code binds only when a law, contract or policy imposes it.
Final two: C beats A because compliance duties follow the activities an organization carries out, so a new activity can bring requirements beyond its founding law.
Exam cue: on CIA questions, when an organization starts a new activity, ask which laws, contracts or rules come with it before judging its compliance coverage.

questions.subtopic: 1C8 Control design, effectiveness and efficiency. A report that no one acts on
questions.question: An Algerian distributor's credit manager, who must review a report of sales above credit limits, has not opened it since May; two such buyers paid late. Which conclusion by internal auditor Leila Benali is BEST?

options.A: Effective: the system produces the report on schedule as designed
options.B: Design inadequate: the system reports such sales instead of blocking them
options.C: Not effective: two buyers above their limits have since paid late
options.D: Not effective: no one performs the review that acts on the report

questions.key_concept: A detective control works only through its follow-up: a report of exceptions that no one reviews leaves the control not operating effectively.
questions.pre_read: Which part of this control manages the risk: the report, or the review that acts on it?
questions.correct_explanation: The glossary defines a control as an action taken to manage risk. The report only lists exceptions; the control is the credit manager's review that acts on them, and it has not happened since May, so the control is not operating effectively. The closest choice blames the design, but a review of exceptions can be a sound detective design; the facts show it is not being performed.

wrong_explanations.B: Closest choice: blocking such sales may suit some risks better, but a detective review can be an adequate design. The facts show the review is skipped, an operating failure.
wrong_explanations.A: A report running on schedule is only the first half of a detective control. Without the review that follows up each exception, nothing manages the risk.
wrong_explanations.C: The verdict fits but the reason does not: late payment can follow even a reviewed sale. The control fails because no one performs the review.

tips: Eliminate: A, because a report no one reviews manages no risk, and C, because late payment is an outcome, which does not show whether the control was performed.
Final two: D beats B because the design, a review of exceptions, can work; the failure is that no one performs it, which is an operating failure.
Exam cue: on CIA questions, a detective control is the follow-up action, not the report. Judge it by whether someone acts on the exceptions, not by outcomes.

questions.subtopic: 1C4 Types of risk. Outside factors in inherent risk
questions.question: A Bangladeshi garment maker's register leaves floods out of its riverside warehouse's inherent risk, as no manager can prevent them. Which view by internal auditor Nusrat Jahan is MOST accurate?

options.A: Floods belong in inherent risk, which counts outside factors too
options.B: Floods stay out of inherent risk, as managers cannot prevent them
options.C: Floods belong in residual risk alone, once insurance is counted
options.D: Floods belong in the continuity plan rather than the risk register

questions.key_concept: Inherent risk combines internal and external risk factors before any management action, so exposures that managers cannot prevent still count.
questions.pre_read: Does inherent risk include only what managers can influence, or outside factors as well?
questions.correct_explanation: The Standards' glossary defines inherent risk as the mix of internal and external risk factors present when management has taken no action. Flooding is an external factor, so it belongs in the warehouse's inherent risk whether or not managers can prevent it; insurance and continuity plans are management's actions and count in residual risk. The closest choice confuses what management can prevent with what the exposure is.

wrong_explanations.B: Closest choice: managers cannot stop floods, but inherent risk measures exposure before any action, from inside and outside the organization. Factors no one controls are part of it.
wrong_explanations.C: Insurance is a management action, so it does lower residual risk. The flood exposure still starts in inherent risk, before insurance is counted.
wrong_explanations.D: A continuity plan is one response to floods, and the warehouse may need one. The exposure still belongs in the register, where inherent and residual risk are rated.

tips: Eliminate: C, because insurance lowers residual risk but the exposure starts in inherent risk, and D, because a continuity plan answers a risk that the register still shows.
Final two: A beats B because inherent risk includes external factors before any management action; whether managers can prevent an event does not decide whether it is a risk.
Exam cue: on CIA questions, inherent risk asks what could happen with no management action, from inside or outside. Controllability shapes the response, not the inherent rating.

questions.subtopic: 1C6 Risk management across the organization. Ratings set by those whose bonus depends on them
questions.question: At an Indonesian palm-oil group, unit heads rate their units' risks, and part of each head's bonus needs a green risk profile. Which view of the ratings by internal auditor Dewi Lestari is MOST accurate?

options.A: Reliable: every unit applies the group's approved method and scale
options.B: Not reliable as they stand: the bonus rule biases the raters
options.C: Not reliable until internal audit takes over rating the top risks
options.D: Reliable: the bonus rule rewards heads who bring their risks down

questions.key_concept: Risk ratings are only as reliable as the raters' objectivity: a reward tied to self-reported ratings invites rating low, whatever method is used.
questions.pre_read: What earns the bonus: a lower risk, or a lower rating that the heads give themselves?
questions.correct_explanation: The IIA's 2026 statement on enterprise risk management says assurance covers how risk culture shapes incentives and accountability, and its Three Lines statement notes that owning a process limits first-line objectivity. A bonus tied to a green profile rewards heads for their own low ratings, not for risk actually reduced, so the ratings cannot be taken as they stand. The closest choice reads the bonus as rewarding real risk reduction.

wrong_explanations.A: One approved method and scale is part of sound rating. Applied by raters with a reason to rate low, it still yields ratings that cannot be taken as they stand.
wrong_explanations.C: Internal audit should validate key risks for its plan, but taking over some ratings would leave the rest biased and have it audit its own work.
wrong_explanations.D: Closest choice: an incentive to cut real risk would help. This bonus turns on a profile the heads rate themselves, so low ratings earn it as surely as low risk.

tips: Eliminate: A, because a sound method cannot correct raters who gain from low ratings, and C, because internal audit validates key risks for its plan but does not take over management's register.
Final two: B beats D because the bonus attaches to the ratings the heads give themselves, not to risk actually reduced, so it rewards rating low.
Exam cue: on CIA questions, ask whether the people producing risk information gain from what it says. An incentive tied to self-reported ratings makes them unreliable.
